title: Anthropic Claude Platform: Agent Skills overview
claims_supported: Agent Skills are modular capabilities containing instructions, metadata, and optional resources.
Skills use three-level progressive disclosure: metadata, SKILL.md instructions, resources/code.
Security considerations include auditing bundled files, scripts, network calls, and tool misuse.
limitations: Claude-specific documentation; not a general standard for all agent runtimes.

title: Anthropic Claude Platform: Skill authoring best practices
claims_supported: Good Skills are concise, well-structured, and tested with real usage.
Description should describe what the Skill does and when to use it.
SKILL.md should usually stay under 500 lines and use progressive disclosure.
Effective Skills use workflows, validation loops, scripts, concrete examples, and evals.
limitations: Authoring guidance; does not define the local D1-D8 framework.

title: Anthropic Engineering: Equipping agents for the real world with Agent Skills
claims_supported: Agent Skills package procedural knowledge and organizational context.
Skill directories include SKILL.md plus optional scripts and resources.
Start from evaluation, structure for scale, think from the agent perspective, and audit security.
limitations: Engineering blog; useful for design intent but not a formal conformance specification.

title: Claude.ai Documentation: Creating custom skills
claims_supported: Custom skills solve specific repeatable tasks, define when they should be used, and focus on one workflow.
Directory name should match the name field.
Validate skills with skills-ref and test trigger behavior after upload.
limitations: Claude.ai consumer/product surface; some constraints differ from API and Codex.

title: Agent Skills open standard: Specification
claims_supported: A skill is a directory containing SKILL.md.
Required frontmatter fields are name and description.
Optional directories include scripts, references, and assets.
allowed-tools is optional and experimental.
Progressive disclosure and one-level file references are recommended.
limitations: Open standard documentation; includes implementation-neutral guidance, not local repo policy.

title: Agent Skills open standard: Best practices for skill creators
claims_supported: Effective skills should come from real expertise and real execution traces.
Skills should spend context wisely and use progressive disclosure.
Skills should favor procedures, defaults, gotchas, templates, checklists, validation loops, and reusable scripts.
limitations: Best-practice guide, not a mandatory compliance standard.

title: Agent Skills open standard: Evaluating skill output quality
claims_supported: Skill quality should be tested with realistic prompts and expected outputs.
Run with-skill and without-skill baselines.
Require concrete evidence for PASS and aggregate benchmark results.
limitations: Describes eval workflow; does not mandate exact thresholds for all organizations.

title: OpenAI Developers: Agent Skills in Codex
claims_supported: Skills extend Codex with task-specific capabilities and build on the open Agent Skills standard.
Codex uses progressive disclosure and can activate skills explicitly or implicitly.
Descriptions should have clear scope and trigger words.
Codex supports agents/openai.yaml for UI metadata, invocation policy, and dependencies.
Best practices include focused skills, imperative steps, explicit inputs/outputs, and testing prompts against descriptions.
limitations: Codex-specific; not all fields are portable across runtimes.

title: OpenAI Developers: Custom instructions with AGENTS.md
claims_supported: Codex loads layered instruction files before work.
Instruction discovery has precedence and size limits.
Persistent guidance and scoped overrides are part of Codex customization.
limitations: AGENTS.md is adjacent to Skills but not the same artifact.

title: OpenAI Developers: Codex subagents
claims_supported: Codex can spawn specialized subagents in parallel when explicitly requested.
Custom agents should be narrow, opinionated, have matching tool surfaces, and avoid adjacent drift.
limitations: Subagents are adjacent runtime machinery, not Skill format requirements.

title: OpenAI Developers: Codex configuration reference
claims_supported: Codex config supports skills.config path/enabled entries.
Codex configuration includes sandbox, approval, permissions, agents, hooks, and project instruction settings.
limitations: Configuration reference; does not define quality criteria by itself.

title: GitHub Docs: Adding agent skills for GitHub Copilot CLI
claims_supported: Copilot agent skills are folders of instructions, scripts, and resources.
description defines what the skill does and when Copilot should use it.
allowed-tools can pre-approve tools, but shell/bash preapproval has security risk.
Skills are for relevant detailed instructions; custom instructions are for simple broadly relevant guidance.
limitations: GitHub Copilot-specific implementation; useful as ecosystem comparison.

title: Anthropic GitHub repository: anthropics/skills
claims_supported: Skills are folders of instructions, scripts, and resources that Claude loads dynamically.
Each skill is self-contained with SKILL.md.
Repository examples are demonstration and educational, and should be tested before critical use.
limitations: Example repository; README disclaims production behavior equivalence.

title: OpenAI GitHub repository: openai/skills
claims_supported: OpenAI maintains a Skills Catalog for Codex.
Agent Skills are folders of instructions, scripts, and resources.
Codex uses skills to package repeatable task capabilities.
limitations: Catalog and examples; not a full quality standard.

title: arXiv: Agent Skills: A Data-Driven Analysis of Claude Skills for Extending Large Language Model Functionality
claims_supported: Large-scale public skills show concentration, redundancy, heavy-tailed length distribution, and safety risks.
Skills are emerging infrastructure for agents and require standardization and safety-aware design.
limitations: arXiv preprint; marketplace sample may not represent private enterprise skills.

title: arXiv: Malicious Or Not: Adding Repository Context to Agent Skill Classification
claims_supported: Security analysis of agent skills should consider repository context, not only SKILL.md descriptions.
Skill ecosystem has real attack vectors including abandoned repository hijacking.
Description-only scanners can overclassify or misclassify risk.
limitations: arXiv preprint; exact scanner results may depend on dataset and methodology.

title: arXiv: Graph of Skills: Dependency-Aware Structural Retrieval for Massive Agent Skills
claims_supported: Large skill libraries create context-window, token cost, hallucination, and latency challenges.
Context-budgeted retrieval and dependency-aware hydration can improve skill use at scale.
limitations: arXiv preprint; not a direct standard for authoring individual first-party skills.

title: Local file: shared/reference/Skill质量标准.md
claims_supported: Defines local first-party Skill runtime quality dimensions D1-D8.
Requires evidence-backed PASS/FAIL/COMMENT findings.
Separates JSON machine fact source from Markdown/HTML derived views.
limitations: Local standard under review; not an external authority.

title: Local file: shared/reference/Skill能力有效性标准.md
claims_supported: Separates Skill effectiveness from runtime quality.
Defines capability_uplift, encoded_preference, mixed eval types.
Requires evals and lifecycle review records.
limitations: Contains a noted consistency gap around next_action example fields.

title: Local file: shared/reference/Skill生命周期管理.md
claims_supported: Defines lifecycle gates for launch, model upgrade, periodic review, and retirement.
States lifecycle management does not add D1-D8 dimensions.
Requires manual confirmation before retirement.
limitations: Needs tighter cross-reference with effectiveness schema and local validators.

title: Local file: README.md
claims_supported: Defines repository structure, first-party and community source locations, install order, and validation commands.
Shows shared/ as first-party truth area.
limitations: Does not explicitly list the three Skill standard files in the current truth-source section.
